posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I'd much prefer SotM to end before it jumps the shark rather than going down the make-way-too-many-expansions-because-fans-will-keep-buying-them route that some other games have taken. More is not always better. Don't get me wrong, I love SotM, but I would hate to see it reach the stage where new heroes start to get repetitive and/or boring because all the good deck ideas have been used already.

And I'm really looking forward to seeing how all the plot threads come together as the story arc finishes. I don't want to wait for years to find that out while the game gets needlessly expanded.

I recommend checking out the many fan-made decks available on BGG if you want more stuff. The Cauldron fan expansion gets a lot of love over there - I have most of that myself and find the heroes to be quite fun. The villains are less well-designed but still interesting, and the environments can be pretty brutal so might be worth considering them if you want to make easy villains more challenging.

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked:
But it's not coming to an end. We'll be able to play it pretty-much forever. 

There are a lot of choices available with the sets we already have. And we're going to get a set to fill-out the Vengeance-style options, along with another set on top of everything!

Plus, coming out of the villain context (way-back-when) I created my own villain (with a related environment) and a friend also created one, so we have those to play with. I'm not big on fan-made content, but at some point I might check out other options.  

I'll admit I'm a little worried about how the final set will introduce a new play style, but I trust the GtG folks to deliver interesting stuff, so we'll see how it works out.
